title: Etale affine qcoherent acyclicity in successor degree
statement: For every natural number n, higher etale cohomology in degree n+1 of the associated quasi-coherent sheaf on an affine scheme is subsingleton.

proof.text: Fix $X=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ and let $\mathcal B$ be the affine objects of the small etale site $X_{\mathrm{et}}$. Let $\mathrm{Cov}$ consist of finite jointly surjective families of etale maps from affine schemes to an affine object $U\in\mathcal B$. For a family in $\mathrm{Cov}$, every iterated fibre product is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. Thus $U$, its members, and all iterated fibre products lie in $\mathcal B$, verifying condition (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-cech-vanishing-criterion]. Every etale covering of an affine $U$ has a refinement in $\mathrm{Cov}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-affine-refinement], so condition (2), cofinality, holds.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03F9 (label lemma-cech-vanish-collection), hypotheses (1) and (2); Schemes Lemmas Tags 01I4/01JQ and Topologies Lemma Tag 0218

proof.text: For a family $\mathcal U=(U_j\to U)$ in $\mathrm{Cov}$, with $u:U\to X$ the structure map, set $V=\coprod_jU_j$. The pullback $u^*\mathcal F$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_U$-module by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent], so $(u^*\mathcal F)_{\mathrm{et}}$ is an abelian sheaf on $U_{\mathrm{et}}$ by [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module] and [lem-sc-etale-qcoherent-descent]. For an object $g:W\to U$ of $U_{\mathrm{et}}$ (an object $u\circ g$ of $X_{\mathrm{et}}$), the composition isomorphism $c_{g,u}:g^*u^*\mathcal F\cong(u\circ g)^*\mathcal F$ of [lem-pc-module-pullback-identity-composition] gives $\Gamma(W,g^*u^*\mathcal F)\cong\Gamma(W,(u\circ g)^*\mathcal F)=\mathcal F_{\mathrm{et}}(W)$, compatibly with the restrictions $\rho$ of [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module] (the maps $\rho_g$ are defined through these $c$'s); since fibre products over $U$ are the same in $U_{\mathrm{et}}$ and $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], the Cech complex of $\mathcal U$ for $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{et}}$ in $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ is that of $\mathcal U$ for $(u^*\mathcal F)_{\mathrm{et}}$ in $U_{\mathrm{et}}$. The standard-cover comparison [lem-sc-etale-standard-cover-cech], applied to the affine scheme $U$ and the sheaf $(u^*\mathcal F)_{\mathrm{et}}$, identifies this Cech complex with the one-map Cech complex of $V\to U$ and gives that $A\to B$ is faithfully flat, where $U=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$, $V=\operatorname{Spec}(B)$. With $M=\Gamma(U,u^*\mathcal F)$, [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] and [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] (applied to the quasi-coherent $u^*\mathcal F$ on the affine $U$) identify the terms on $V^{p+1}_U$ with $M\otimes_A B^{\otimes_A(p+1)}$. The pullback identity and composition [lem-pc-module-pullback-identity-composition], together with the definition [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module], identify all face maps with the Amitsur differentials. Therefore [lem-pc-cech-exact] gives $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F_{\mathrm{et}})=0$ for every $p>0$, verifying condition (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-cech-vanishing-criterion]. For the Lean realization, lift every section group and every map to the coefficient universe u+1. Products of finitely indexed section groups, kernels, and images identify with their lifts, so the Amitsur exactness applies unchanged: an underlying cocycle has an underlying preimage, and lifting the preimage proves exactness of the lifted complex.

source.place: Theorem Tag 03P2 (label theorem-zariski-fpqc-quasi-coherent), affine case, Cech/Amitsur calculation; Lemma Tag 03OZ (label lemma-cech-complex)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-cech-vanishing-criterion] with $\mathcal F=\mathcal F_{\mathrm{et}}$ and $U=X$ (an affine object of $X_{\mathrm{et}}$, so in $\mathcal B$). It yields $H^q(X,\mathcal F_{\mathrm{et}})=0$ for $q>0$, where $H^q(X,-)$ is the $q$-th right derived functor, computed by an injective resolution $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{et}}\to I^\bullet$ in $\Ab(X_{\mathrm{et}})$, of evaluation at the final object $X$, which is the global-sections functor $\Gamma(X,-)$ [def-weil-pbc-global-sections-functor]. The injective resolution $I^\bullet$ is a bounded-below complex of injective objects, hence K-injective, so $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{et}}\to I^\bullet$ is a K-injective resolution [prop-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. By [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], $H^q(X_{\mathrm{et}},\mathcal F_{\mathrm{et}})=\mathcal H^q(\Gamma(X,I^\bullet))=H^q(X,\mathcal F_{\mathrm{et}})$. Hence $H^q(X_{\mathrm{et}},\mathcal F_{\mathrm{et}})=0$ for every $q>0$.
